introduction: Panchayati Raj is a system of rural local self-government in India. Its main objective is to ensure 'Democratic Decentralization' and build democracy at the grassroots level. It is based on Mahatma Gandhi's vision of 'Gram Swaraj' (Village Self-rule).

core_concepts.title: 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992)
core_concepts.description: This is the most important act for PRIs. It granted 'Constitutional Status' to Panchayati Raj institutions. It added a new 'Part IX' to the Constitution and the '11th Schedule'.

core_concepts.title: Three-Tier System
core_concepts.description: The act provides for a 3-tier system of Panchayati Raj in every state: 1. Gram Panchayat (at the village level), 2. Panchayat Samiti (at the intermediate/block level), and 3. Zila Parishad (at the district level).

core_concepts.title: Age and Tenure
core_concepts.description: The minimum age to contest panchayat elections is '21 years' (unlike 25 years for MLAs/MPs). The normal tenure of a panchayat is 5 years. If dissolved earlier, fresh elections must be held within 6 months.

core_concepts.title: The First Panchayat
core_concepts.description: In independent India, the Panchayati Raj system was first established in the 'Nagaur' district of Rajasthan on October 2, 1959, inaugurated by PM Jawaharlal Nehru. Andhra Pradesh was the second state to adopt it.

important_entities.name: Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957)
important_entities.significance: Balwant Rai Mehta is often called the 'Architect of Panchayati Raj in India' because his committee originally recommended the establishment of the democratic decentralized three-tier system.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Students often confuse the two. Remember: The age to VOTE in a panchayat election is 18 years, but the minimum age to CONTEST the election is 21 years.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Gram Panchayat (Village), Panchayat Samiti (Block/Intermediate), Zila Parishad (District).

exam_strategy_tips: The 73rd Amendment Act (1992) and the 11th Schedule are the most frequently tested facts at the beginner level.
Always remember the location of the first panchayat: Nagaur, Rajasthan (1959).
